request: why is a longer password so much harder to guess?

beats.intent: Four boxes for a 4-letter password, each with 26 choices
beats.narration: A password of four lowercase letters: each box can hold any of twenty six letters.
beats.code:
stage.title("Password length")
boxes = VGroup(*[Square(1.0, color=BLUE) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).move_to([0, 0.6, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(b) for b in boxes], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(boxes)
for b in boxes:
    t = Text("26", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).move_to(b)
    stage.add(t)
    stage.play(FadeIn(t), run_time=0.3)

beats.narration: Multiply the choices: twenty six to the fourth, under half a million. A computer tries that in a blink.

beats.intent: Bars of the number of digits in the count for 4, 8 and 12 letters: 6, 12 and 17
beats.narration: Each extra letter multiplies the count by twenty six. Eight letters give a twelve digit number; twelve letters, seventeen digits.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [6, 12, 17], labels=["4 letters", "8 letters", "12 letters"], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("digits in the number of possible passwords")

request: how does a map scale work?

beats.intent: A map rectangle with two towns 4 cm apart and a scale bar 1 : 50 000
beats.narration: On this map two towns are four centimetres apart. The scale says one to fifty thousand.
beats.code:
stage.title("Reading a map scale")
m = draw_rectangle(stage, width=7, height=4, color=GREEN, fill=0.15)
a = Dot([-2, 0, 0], color=RED, radius=0.12)
b = Dot([2, 0, 0], color=RED, radius=0.12)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(a), GrowFromCenter(b))
stage.add(a, b)
stage.label(a, "Ashby", direction=UP, color=RED)
stage.label(b, "Brook", direction=UP, color=RED)
d = draw_arrow(stage, (-2, -0.5), (2, -0.5), color=YELLOW, label="4 cm")
stage.caption("scale 1 : 50 000")

beats.intent: The map beside 4 cm × 50 000 = 200 000 cm = 2 km
beats.narration: Every centimetre on the map is fifty thousand centimetres on the ground. Four centimetres is two hundred thousand centimetres: two kilometres.

beats.intent: A winding 6 cm road on the map beside 6 cm → 3 km
beats.narration: The road between them winds, and measures six centimetres on the map: three kilometres to drive.
beats.code:
A, B = a.get_center(), b.get_center()
k = (B - A)[0] / 4
road = VMobject(color=ORANGE, stroke_width=5).set_points_smoothly([A, A + k * np.array([1, 1.2, 0]), A + k * np.array([2.5, -1.0, 0]), B])
stage.play(Create(road))
stage.add(road)
stage.equation(r"6\ \text{cm} \to 6 \times 0.5\ \text{km} = 3\ \text{km}")

request: how does a hash table find things so fast?

beats.intent: Seven numbered bucket boxes in a row, 0 to 6
beats.narration: A hash table is a row of buckets, here seven of them.
beats.code:
stage.title("A hash table")
buckets = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.9, color=GREY_B) for _ in range(7)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).move_to([0, -0.8, 0])
stage.play(Create(buckets))
stage.add(buckets)
nums = VGroup(*[Text(str(k), font_size=22, color=GREY_B).next_to(bk, DOWN, buff=0.1) for k, bk in enumerate(buckets)])
stage.play(FadeIn(nums))
stage.add(nums)

beats.intent: The keys 15, 23 and 40 each dropped into bucket key mod 7: 1, 2 and 5
beats.narration: To store a number, divide by seven and keep the remainder. Fifteen goes in bucket one, twenty three in bucket two, forty in bucket five.
beats.code:
for key, slot in ((15, 1), (23, 2), (40, 5)):
    t = Text(str(key), font_size=30, color=YELLOW).move_to([buckets[slot].get_x(), 1.6, 0])
    stage.play(FadeIn(t))
    stage.play(t.animate.move_to(buckets[slot]), run_time=0.6)
    stage.add(t)
stage.caption("bucket = key mod 7")

beats.intent: A search for 23 jumping straight to bucket 2, which is lit
beats.narration: To find twenty three later, don't search: work out the bucket, two, and look only there.

request: how high does a ball go if I throw it up at 20 m/s?

beats.intent: Axes of time and height with the curve h = 20t - 5t² from 0 to 4 seconds
beats.narration: Throw a ball straight up at twenty metres a second. Gravity slows it by ten metres a second, every second.
beats.code:
stage.title("A ball thrown up")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 4), y_range=(0, 25), labels=("seconds", "metres"))
h = lambda t: 20 * t - 5 * t ** 2
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, h, x_range=(0, 4), color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: A dot riding the curve up to the top at (2, 20) and back down
beats.narration: It rises, slows, stops for an instant at the top, and falls back.
beats.code:
trace_graph(stage, ax, h, 0, 4)
top = mark_point(stage, ax, (2, 20), color=YELLOW, label="(2, 20)")

beats.intent: The curve beside: speed 0 at t = 2, so h = 20·2 - 5·2² = 20 m
beats.narration: It stops when its speed, twenty minus ten t, reaches zero: at two seconds. The height then is twenty metres.
